## So what is the composable unit?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A `Distributions.jl` distribution is already an interface the whole of
  Julia understands, so write the epidemiology as distributions and the
  probabilistic programming language becomes optional
- `CensoredDistributions.jl` does not depend on Turing. Nothing in
  `src/` mentions it
- It does not depend on `ConvolvedDistributions.jl` either. They compose
  through `Distributions.jl`

::: {.callout-important}
The delay half of this has a story, the time series half and the
fitting layer do not.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```julia
# a serial interval, censored and truncated
si = double_interval_censored(
  convolve_distributions(generation_time, incubation);
  upper = 15, interval = 1)

typeof(si)
# IntervalCensored{Truncated{PrimaryCensored{Convolved{…}}}}

cdf(si, 5.0)   # 0.094
```

::: {.attribution}
`CensoredDistributions.jl` v0.2.22, run for this talk,
`scripts/composable-composed-type.jl`. The type is that script's output
with the parameter types dropped, and `cdf` needed no telling about it ·
Neither package appears in the other's `[deps]`, checked in each
`Project.toml` · Open issue `CensoredDistributions.jl#749` says the
joint fit is too slow, because reverse mode autodiff through
`cdf(Convolved(...))` costs too much per step ·
[samabbott.co.uk/JuliaCon2026/delays][delays-talk]
:::
:::
::::

## Is JAX the way forward, and is Julia the place?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**JAX**

- In the paper I wrote that NumPyro and JAX are promising, with barriers
  for epidemiological modellers, and that I find them ugly. Taste is not
  an argument
- One autodiff system, and everything is written against it
- We test six configurations and still cannot tell a user which one is
  safe for a model built from five packages
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Julia**

- Multiple dispatch is why a composed delay is still a distribution. I
  do not know how to write that as cleanly anywhere else
- The teams under Turing, under the autodiff backends, and under our own
  packages are all small
- The infectious disease ecosystem here is smaller again
:::
::::

::: {.callout-important}
I have argued myself into both answers, and I would like a reason to
prefer one.
:::

::: {.attribution}
The alternative approaches, including NumPyro and JAX, are in the
paper's discussion,
[epiaware.org/approaches](https://epiaware.org/approaches/)
· The six autodiff configurations were the 14:30 talk in this room,
[samabbott.co.uk/JuliaCon2026/roadmap](https://samabbott.co.uk/JuliaCon2026/roadmap/)
:::
